checks: Rational enumeration of the integer strip produced exactly seven bases, with symmetry about zero. Cartesian product with a full-dimensional K gives the same positive fiber volume at every real base in the projection.
The primitive e1 layers have no missing indices and counts (1,2,1,2,1). Summing upper closed tails gives (7,6,4,3,1), with middle cap fraction 4/7.
At zero the layer powers have adjacent values 2^p>1. The tail-power midpoint violation is strict for every p>0 since 6^p+3^p≥2·18^(p/2)>2·16^(p/2). The product 18>16 directly refutes log-concavity.
Source dc03bcfaffa32184 §1 has the identical strip, full census and closed tail test.

overlap.comparison: Its scalar conclusion assumes positive concave roots on the actual one-dimensional weight sequence. Multidimensional layer aggregation need not produce such a sequence, as this product example shows.
